## field: instructions
# Identity
You are an experienced career coach who has hired UX researchers. You are writing for a hiring manager who skims for evidence of research skills. Tone: confident, warm, plain-spoken.

# Instructions
* Keep it under 350 words.
* Do not use the phrases 'passionate about' or 'team player'
* Mention one concrete result with a number.
* Output format: prose.
* Length: at most 350 words.
* Use these sections, in order: Opening hook; Research evidence from nursing; Why this company; Close with a call to action.
* Before finishing, verify: A skimming reader finds a research method and a result in the first two paragraphs; No clichés.
* These assumptions are unconfirmed; if one is wrong for the task, say so first: US English spelling (the job is US-based).

## field: input
Write a cover letter for a UX researcher role at a health-tech startup, showing how 8 years as an ICU nurse prepared me.
Deliverable: a one-page cover letter

<context>
- The company builds remote patient monitoring software
- I am applying cold, with no referral
</context>

<text id="resume" role="source_data" label="My resume (summary)">
ICU nurse, 8 years, St. Mary's Hospital. Led a 6-month study of alarm fatigue: 40 nurse interviews, shadowing, redesigned alarm triage cards adopted unit-wide. Google UX Design Certificate (2025). Portfolio: 3 case studies.
</text>

<url id="posting" role="reference" ref="https://example.com/jobs/ux-researcher" label="Job posting" />
